note: Independent georeferencing check against a hand-measured crater catalogue. Criterion written and committed BEFORE any offset was measured. Only catalogue counts per diameter bin were looked at to choose the range.

catalogue.name: Robbins lunar crater database v1, 2018-08-15 (USGS Astrogeology, PDS4 bundle, 1,296,796 records)
catalogue.how_independent: Positions were measured by hand on LROC WAC images, LOLA topography, Kaguya TC images and the merged LOLA+TC DTM, in a LOLA control net (USGS page). It is therefore NOT independent of LOLA: this check tests our reading and georeferencing of the LDEM files against LOLA-controlled products, not the absolute lunar frame.
catalogue.centre_used: LAT_CIRC_IMG, LON_CIRC_IMG (circle fit to the rim), diameter DIAM_CIRC_IMG

selection.region: centre latitude <= -80.5 deg and centre distance from the pole + 1.5 * radius <= 300 km, so the whole rim and its search window lie inside the 20 m product
selection.diameter_range_km: 2 <= D < 16. Below 2 km the rim is under 100 pixels of 20 m across and the catalogue's own positional error is a large fraction of the crater; above 16 km craters are rare (under 100 in the region), old and irregular, and a single large crater has too much leverage.
quality_flags: DIAM_ELLI_ELLIP_IMG <= 1.1 (near circular, so a circle is a fair model of the rim)
ARC_IMG >= 0.8 (at least 80 % of the rim arc was measured, i.e. a clear rim)

rim_fit.rays: 72 azimuths every 5 deg from the catalogue centre in the polar stereographic plane; plane radius of the catalogue circle a = (D/2) * k, k = 1 / cos^2(colatitude / 2) the projection scale
rim_fit.crest: highest 20 m DEM point (bilinear, 10 m steps) on each ray between 0.75 a and 1.25 a
rim_fit.circle: algebraic least-squares circle through the crest points; points with |residual| > 3 * 1.4826 * MAD are dropped and the circle is refitted once
crater_accepted_if: at least 50 of the 72 rays kept
root-mean-square residual of kept points <= 0.06 a
rim_fit.offset: fitted centre minus catalogue centre, (dx, dy) in metres in the polar stereographic plane

estimation.model: t_i = T + delta * (z x r_i) + eps * r_i, with r_i the catalogue centre relative to the pole, T = (Tx, Ty) common translation, delta rotation about the pole, eps radial scale
estimation.fit: ordinary least squares over all accepted craters; craters whose residual vector is longer than 3 * 1.4826 * MAD of the residual lengths are dropped and the fit repeated once
estimation.standard_errors: bootstrap over craters, 1000 resamples, standard deviation of each parameter
estimation.stability: leave-one-out largest change of each parameter; the same fit separately on craters with longitude < 180 and >= 180, and on craters nearer and farther than the median distance from the pole

what_matters_for_horizons.translation_why: a 1 km high ridge 5 km away shifted by 100 m changes its elevation angle by about 0.2 degree, a large part of the 0.53 degree solar disc
what_matters_for_horizons.rotation_why: 0.038 deg moves a point 150 km from the pole (the farthest of the three sites is about 120 km) by 100 m

classification.detected: |estimate| >= 3 * bootstrap SE AND the estimate has the same sign in both longitude halves and in both distance halves (for the translation: both components)
classification.ruled_out_to_matter_level: not detected AND |estimate| + 1.96 * SE < the 'matters' level
